# Resource: stripe_account_v2

A connected account created through Stripe's `/v2` Accounts API, whose configurations say how the platform uses it: as a customer, a merchant or a recipient. Each configuration requests one capability: `automatic_indirect_tax` for a customer, `card_payments` for a merchant and `stripe_balance.stripe_transfers` for a recipient; state holds every configuration the account has applied, with the status of each capability. Stripe refuses `dashboard` on an account that is only a customer. The account is also a v1 connected account with the same ID, which the `stripe_account` data source reads. Set `closed` to `true` to close the account, which cannot be undone; Stripe returns most fields of a closed account as null, so state keeps the values they had before the close. Stripe refuses any change to a closed account, so once it is closed a plan that changes it fails. `identity.entity_type`, `identity.business_details.registered_name`, `defaults.locales`, `defaults.profile` and the recipient configuration's `capabilities.stripe_balance.stripe_transfers.requested` change in place; changing that `requested` flag can move the status of the recipient's capabilities. Stripe refuses a change of `dashboard` or of the collectors in `defaults.responsibilities` once they are set, so a plan that changes one on an existing account fails, as does one that changes `identity.country`, `defaults.currency`, `configuration.customer`, `configuration.merchant` or the recipient configuration's `applied`, because changing them is not supported yet: revert the configuration, ignore the change, or remove the account from the state and apply again to create a new one. Stripe returns `identity.country` in upper case, so state keeps the country as you configured it. Stripe has no proven way to clear `display_name` or `contact_email`, so an apply that removes one from the configuration fails; removing `dashboard`, `identity.country` or the registered name leaves it on the account, and removing `contact_phone`, `identity.entity_type` or a member of `defaults.profile` clears it.

~> Stripe cannot delete an account created through `/v2`; set `closed` to `true` to close it. `terraform destroy`, and a change that would replace the v2 account, fail at plan time. To stop managing a v2 account, remove it from the state as [Removing from State](#removing-from-state) shows; it stays in the Stripe account.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# A merchant whose platform collects its fees and covers its losses, without a Stripe
# dashboard.
resource "stripe_account_v2" "seller" {
  display_name  = "Acme Supplies"
  contact_email = "payments@acme.example"
  dashboard     = "none"

  identity = {
    country     = "US"
    entity_type = "company"
    business_details = {
      registered_name = "Acme Supplies Inc."
    }
  }

  configuration = {
    merchant = {
      capabilities = {
        card_payments = { requested = true }
      }
    }
  }

  defaults = {
    currency = "usd"
    responsibilities = {
      fees_collector   = "application"
      losses_collector = "application"
    }
  }

  metadata = {
    team = "marketplace"
  }
}
```

## Argument Reference

The following arguments are optional:

* `closed` - (Optional) Indicates whether the account has been closed. Possible values: `true`. Removing it from the configuration stops sending it, and the next apply records the value Stripe holds.
* `configuration` - (Optional) An Account Configuration which allows the Account to take on a key persona across Stripe products. Removing it from the configuration leaves the current value. See [`configuration`](#configuration) below.
* `contact_email` - (Optional) The primary contact email address for the Account. Default: none.
* `contact_phone` - (Optional) The default contact phone for the Account. Default: none.
* `dashboard` - (Optional) A value indicating the Stripe dashboard this Account has access to. This will depend on which configurations are enabled for this account. Possible values: `express`, `full`, `none`. Default: none. Removing it from the configuration leaves the current value.
* `defaults` - (Optional) Default values to be used on Account Configurations. Removing it from the configuration leaves the current value. See [`defaults`](#defaults) below.
* `display_name` - (Optional) A descriptive name for the Account. This name will be surfaced in the Stripe Dashboard and on any invoices sent to the Account. Default: none.
* `identity` - (Optional) Information about the company, individual, and business represented by the Account. Removing it from the configuration leaves the current value. See [`identity`](#identity) below.
* `metadata` - (Optional) Set of key-value pairs that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format. Default (Stripe): `{}`.

<a id="configuration"></a>
### `configuration`

The `configuration` attribute supports:

* `customer` - (Optional) The Customer Configuration allows the Account to be used in inbound payment flows (i.e. customer-facing payment and billing flows). See [`configuration.customer`](#configuration.customer) below.
* `merchant` - (Optional) Enables the Account to act as a connected account and collect payments facilitated by a Connect platform. You must onboard your platform to Connect before you can add this configuration to your connected accounts. Utilize this configuration when the Account will be the Merchant of Record, like with Direct charges or Destination Charges with on_behalf_of set. See [`configuration.merchant`](#configuration.merchant) below.
* `recipient` - (Optional) The Recipient Configuration allows the Account to receive funds. Utilize this configuration if the Account will not be the Merchant of Record, like with Separate Charges & Transfers, or Destination Charges without on_behalf_of set. See [`configuration.recipient`](#configuration.recipient) below.

<a id="configuration.customer"></a>
### `configuration.customer`

The `configuration.customer` attribute supports:

* `applied` - (Read-Only) Indicates whether the customer configuration is active. You can deactivate or reactivate the customer configuration by updating this property. Deactivating the configuration by setting this value to false will unrequest all capabilities within the configuration. It will not delete any of the configuration's other properties.
* `capabilities` - (Optional) Capabilities that have been requested on the Customer Configuration. See [`configuration.customer.capabilities`](#configuration.customer.capabilities) below.

<a id="configuration.customer.capabilities"></a>
### `configuration.customer.capabilities`

The `configuration.customer.capabilities` attribute supports:

* `automatic_indirect_tax` - (Optional) Generates requirements for enabling automatic indirect tax calculation on this customer's invoices or subscriptions. Recommended to request this capability if planning to enable automatic tax calculation on this customer's invoices or subscriptions. See [`configuration.customer.capabilities.automatic_indirect_tax`](#configuration.customer.capabilities.automatic_indirect_tax) below.

<a id="configuration.customer.capabilities.automatic_indirect_tax"></a>
### `configuration.customer.capabilities.automatic_indirect_tax`

The `configuration.customer.capabilities.automatic_indirect_tax` attribute supports:

* `requested` - (Required) To request a new Capability for an account, pass true. There can be a delay before the requested Capability becomes active.
* `status` - (Read-Only) The status of the Capability. Possible values: `active`, `pending`, `rejected`, `restricted`, `unsupported`.
* `status_details` - (Read-Only) Additional details about the capability's status. This value is empty when `status` is `active`. See [`configuration.customer.capabilities.automatic_indirect_tax.status_details`](#configuration.customer.capabilities.automatic_indirect_tax.status_details) below.

<a id="configuration.customer.capabilities.automatic_indirect_tax.status_details"></a>
### `configuration.customer.capabilities.automatic_indirect_tax.status_details`

The `configuration.customer.capabilities.automatic_indirect_tax.status_details` attribute is a list. Each element supports:

* `code` - Machine-readable code explaining the reason for the Capability to be in its current status. Possible values: `determining_status`, `rejected_fraud`, `rejected_incomplete_verification`, `rejected_listed`, `rejected_other`, `rejected_platform_fraud`, `rejected_platform_other`, `rejected_platform_terms_of_service`, `rejected_terms_of_service`, `requirements_past_due`, `requirements_pending_verification`, `restricted_other`, `unsupported_business`, `unsupported_country`, `unsupported_entity_type`.
* `resolution` - Machine-readable code explaining how to make the Capability active. Possible values: `contact_stripe`, `no_resolution`, `provide_info`.

<a id="configuration.merchant"></a>
### `configuration.merchant`

The `configuration.merchant` attribute supports:

* `applied` - (Read-Only) Indicates whether the merchant configuration is active. You can deactivate or reactivate the merchant configuration by updating this property. Deactivating the configuration by setting this value to false doesn't delete the configuration's properties.
* `capabilities` - (Optional) Capabilities to request on the Merchant Configuration. See [`configuration.merchant.capabilities`](#configuration.merchant.capabilities) below.

<a id="configuration.merchant.capabilities"></a>

The `configuration.merchant.capabilities` attribute supports:

* `stripe_balance` - (Read-Only) Capabilities that enable the merchant to manage their Stripe Balance (/v1/balance). See [`configuration.merchant.capabilities.stripe_balance`](#configuration.merchant.capabilities.stripe_balance) below.

<a id="defaults"></a>
### `defaults`

The `defaults` attribute supports:

* `currency` - (Optional) Three-letter [ISO currency code](https://www.iso.org/iso-4217-currency-codes.html), in lowercase. Must be a [supported currency](https://stripe.com/docs/currencies). Removing it from the configuration leaves the current value.
* `locales` - (Optional) The Account's preferred locales (languages), ordered by preference. Default (Stripe): `[]`. Removing it from the configuration leaves the current value.
* `profile` - (Optional) Account profile information. Removing it from the configuration leaves the current value. See [`defaults.profile`](#defaults.profile) below.
* `responsibilities` - (Optional) Default responsibilities held by either Stripe or the platform. Removing it from the configuration leaves the current value. See [`defaults.responsibilities`](#defaults.responsibilities) below.

<a id="defaults.profile"></a>
### `defaults.profile`

The `defaults.profile` attribute supports:

* `business_url` - (Optional) The business's publicly-available website. Default: none.
* `doing_business_as` - (Optional) The name which is used by the business. Default: none.
* `product_description` - (Optional) Internal-only description of the product sold or service provided by the business. It's used by Stripe for risk and underwriting purposes. Default: none.

<a id="defaults.responsibilities"></a>
### `defaults.responsibilities`

The `defaults.responsibilities` attribute supports:

* `fees_collector` - (Required) A value indicating the party responsible for collecting fees from this account. Possible values: `application`, `application_custom`, `application_express`, `stripe`.
* `losses_collector` - (Required) A value indicating who is responsible for losses when this Account can’t pay back negative balances from payments. Possible values: `application`, `stripe`.
* `requirements_collector` - (Read-Only) A value indicating responsibility for collecting requirements on this account. Possible values: `application`, `stripe`.

<a id="identity"></a>
### `identity`

The `identity` attribute supports:

* `business_details` - (Optional) Information about the company or business. Removing it from the configuration leaves the current value. See [`identity.business_details`](#identity.business_details) below.
* `country` - (Optional) The country in which the account holder resides, or in which the business is legally established. This should be an [ISO 3166-1 alpha-2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_3166-1_alpha-2) country code. Default: none. Removing it from the configuration leaves the current value.
* `entity_type` - (Optional) The entity type represented by the Account. Ensure this field is accurate before adding configurations that rely on identity information, as it determines which identity fields apply and how the Account is validated. Possible values: `company`, `government_entity`, `individual`, `non_profit`. Default: none.

<a id="identity.business_details"></a>
### `identity.business_details`

The `identity.business_details` attribute supports:

* `registered_name` - (Optional) The business legal name. Removing it from the configuration stops sending it, and the next apply records the value Stripe holds.

## Attribute Reference

This resource exports the following attributes in addition to the arguments above:

* `id` - Unique identifier for the Account.
* `applied_configurations` - The configurations that have been applied to this account.
* `created` - Time at which the object was created. Represented as a RFC 3339 date & time UTC value in millisecond precision, for example: 2022-09-18T13:22:18.123Z.
* `future_requirements` - Information about the future requirements for the Account that will eventually come into effect, including what information needs to be collected, and by when. See [`future_requirements`](#future_requirements) below.
* `livemode` - Has the value `true` if the object exists in live mode or the value `false` if the object exists in test mode.
* `requirements` - Information about the active requirements for the Account, including what information needs to be collected, and by when. See [`requirements`](#requirements) below.

<a id="future_requirements"></a>
### `future_requirements`

The `future_requirements` attribute supports:

* `entries` - A list of requirements for the Account. See [`future_requirements.entries`](#future_requirements.entries) below.
* `minimum_transition_date` - The time at which the future requirements become effective.
* `summary` - An object containing an overview of requirements for the Account. See [`future_requirements.summary`](#future_requirements.summary) below.

<a id="future_requirements.entries"></a>
### `future_requirements.entries`

The `future_requirements.entries` attribute is a list. Each element supports:

* `awaiting_action_from` - Indicates whether the platform or Stripe is currently responsible for taking action on the requirement. Value can be `user` or `stripe`. Possible values: `stripe`, `user`.
* `description` - Machine-readable string describing the requirement.
* `errors` - Descriptions of why the requirement must be collected, or why the collected information isn't satisfactory to Stripe. See [`future_requirements.entries.errors`](#future_requirements.entries.errors) below.
* `impact` - A hash describing the impact of not collecting the requirement, or Stripe not being able to verify the collected information. See [`future_requirements.entries.impact`](#future_requirements.entries.impact) below.
* `minimum_deadline` - The soonest point when the account will be impacted by not providing the requirement. See [`future_requirements.entries.minimum_deadline`](#future_requirements.entries.minimum_deadline) below.
* `reference` - A reference to the location of the requirement. See [`future_requirements.entries.reference`](#future_requirements.entries.reference) below.
* `requested_reasons` - A list of reasons why Stripe is collecting the requirement. See [`future_requirements.entries.requested_reasons`](#future_requirements.entries.requested_reasons) below.

<a id="future_requirements.entries.errors"></a>
### `future_requirements.entries.errors`

The `future_requirements.entries.errors` attribute is a list. Each element supports:

* `code` - Machine-readable code describing the error. Possible values: `invalid_address_city_state_postal_code`, `invalid_address_cmra_address`, `invalid_address_highway_contract_box`, `invalid_address_private_mailbox`, <a id="future_requirements.entries.reference"></a>

The `future_requirements.entries.reference` attribute supports:

* `inquiry` - If `inquiry` is the type, the inquiry token.

The `future_requirements.summary` attribute supports:

* `minimum_deadline` - The soonest date and time a requirement on the Account will become `past due`. <a id="future_requirements.summary.minimum_deadline"></a>

The `future_requirements.summary.minimum_deadline` attribute supports:

* `status` - The current strictest status of all requirements on the Account. Possible values: `currently_due`, `eventually_due`, `past_due`.
* `time` - The soonest RFC3339 date & time UTC value a requirement can impact the Account.

<a id="requirements"></a>
### `requirements`

The `requirements` attribute supports:

* `entries` - A list of requirements for the Account. See [`requirements.entries`](#requirements.entries) below.
* `summary` - An object containing an overview of requirements for the Account. See [`requirements.summary`](#requirements.summary) below.

<a id="requirements.entries"></a>
### `requirements.entries`

The `requirements.entries` attribute is a list. Each element supports:

* `awaiting_action_from` - Indicates whether the platform or Stripe is currently responsible for taking action on the requirement. Value can be `user` or `stripe`. Possible values: `stripe`, `user`.
* `description` - Machine-readable string describing the requirement.
* `errors` - Descriptions of why the requirement must be collected, or why the collected information isn't satisfactory to Stripe. See [`requirements.entries.errors`](#requirements.entries.errors) below.
* `impact` - A hash describing the impact of not collecting the requirement, or Stripe not being able to verify the collected information. See [`requirements.entries.impact`](#requirements.entries.impact) below.
* `minimum_deadline` - The soonest point when the account will be impacted by not providing the requirement. See [`requirements.entries.minimum_deadline`](#requirements.entries.minimum_deadline) below.
* `reference` - A reference to the location of the requirement. See [`requirements.entries.reference`](#requirements.entries.reference) below.
* `requested_reasons` - A list of reasons why Stripe is collecting the requirement. See [`requirements.entries.requested_reasons`](#requirements.entries.requested_reasons) below.

## Timeouts

[Configuration options](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/syntax#operation-timeouts) are set with the `timeouts` attribute, for example `timeouts = { create = "5m" }`:

* `create` - (Default `20m`)
* `delete` - (Default `20m`)
* `update` - (Default `20m`)

## Removing from State

To stop managing a v2 account whose destroy is refused, remove it from the state without destroying it. In Terraform 1.7 and later, and OpenTofu 1.10 and later, replace the `resource` block with a [`removed` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/block/removed) and apply:

```terraform
removed {
  from = stripe_account_v2.seller

  lifecycle {
    destroy = false
  }
}
```

Using `terraform state rm`:

```console
% terraform state rm stripe_account_v2.seller
```

The v2 account stays in the Stripe account. Replacing one with `terraform apply -replace` or `terraform taint` fails in the same way, at apply.

## Import

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, and in OpenTofu, use an [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) to import a v2 account using its ID. For example:

```terraform
import {
  to = stripe_account_v2.seller
  id = "acct_1Nv0FGQ9RKHgCVdK"
}
```

In Terraform v1.12.0 and later, and in OpenTofu v1.12.0 and later, the `import` block can use the `identity` attribute instead. For example:

```terraform
import {
  to = stripe_account_v2.seller
  identity = {
    id = "acct_1Nv0FGQ9RKHgCVdK"
  }
}
```

### Identity Schema

#### Required

* `id` (String) The Stripe ID of the v2 account.

Using `terraform import`, import a v2 account using its ID. For example:

```console
% terraform import stripe_account_v2.seller acct_1Nv0FGQ9RKHgCVdK
```

~> Stripe does not return the capabilities a configuration requested, so an imported account has no `requested` flags in `configuration`, and its `identity.country` is in upper case. Add `lifecycle { ignore_changes = [configuration] }` to a configuration that sets it, because a plan that changes `configuration.customer` or `configuration.merchant` fails, and add `identity.country` to the list if the configuration writes the country in lower case, because a plan that changes it fails too. An imported closed account has no values for the fields Stripe returns as null, and a plan that changes a closed account fails, so its configuration needs `lifecycle { ignore_changes = all }`.
